evidence: All twelve randomized native PNGs visually inspected; all PNG headers verified 1920x1080. Linux OpenGL, MSAA4, renderScale1 and 48m/two-cascade settings were provided in the task, not independently read from hidden metadata before lock. Wind/actors animate; exact leaf geometry is not pixel-matched.
rankingOrder: Best rank group first; labels within a group are tied

cam_hill.confidence: low confidence in a useful quality difference at this distance
cam_hill.reason: All three show a credible green/olive crown with broadly similar separation from the warm background. Small brightness differences do not justify choosing a quality winner. The conspicuous pale blue-gray failure from the earlier Editor hill set does not recur.

cam_hero.confidence: low; a small preference, not a demonstrated major gain
cam_hero.reason: A/C modestly lift the upper-left/interior olive foliage relative to B, giving slightly easier local detail reading while retaining dark main limbs and lit/shaded contrast. I cannot reliably split A/C. Dense overlapping clusters still merge; no gross artificial glow appears.

cam_tree_canopy_below.confidence: moderate for the slight lift over B; low for splitting A/C
cam_tree_canopy_below.reason: A/C make the broad shaded leaves left of the trunk and around smaller embedded branches slightly easier to read. The change is modest. Dense upper-right bundles remain dark textured masses in every variant. Leaf hue stays olive and the brighter versions do not read as emissive.

cam_tree_canopy_edge.confidence: low; small and partly confounded by moving foliage
cam_tree_canopy_edge.reason: A/B provide a slight lift of the central/lower leaf field relative to C. I cannot justify a robust A-versus-B winner. Central clusters still flatten into dense sheets of similar tone, with thin branch lines crossing them. No broad glow or obvious silhouette loss appears.

recommendation: Treat tied brighter candidates as a modest tuning preference only. This evidence does not justify calling shaded canopy complete or selecting one dose conclusively. Preserve repaired edges. Any further change should target actual leaf-plane and cluster response rather than simply adding more uniform brightness; inspect native sun/shade/backlight and moving foliage before accepting it.
remainingDefects: Dense shaded canopy bundles still lack convincing layered depth and differentiated leaf-plane response.
Small embedded branches remain hard to distinguish in the thickest clusters.
Native static edges are cleaner than the prior Editor captures, but leaf-sized detail remains dense and texture-like; motion is unqualified.
Soft shaded bark and broad district art gaps remain outside this material audition.

arkComparison.reason: Stronger differentiated foliage response, plant layering and integration into a much more authored environment. The native leaf tuning is a small improvement far below overall parity.
arkComparison.limitations: Different plant species, composition, lens and lighting; reference settings/hardware/promotional processing unknown. No performance, physics or temporal parity inference.
